children: The $128 bln Air Liquide’s resilient earnings and exposure to the chip boom make it an odd quarry for the cage-ratting firm. Larger rival Linde is doing better, yet the French group is lifting margins and may buy back more shares. Elliott’s challenge is pushing it to aim higher.
Full view will be published shortly.
Follow Yawen Chen on Bluesky and LinkedIn.

Activist investor Elliott Investment Management has built a stake in Paris-based Air Liquide and is urging the French group to improve its margins, Reuters reported on August 31, citing sources familiar with the matter.

Elliott has been engaging with the company for months and is pushing management to make changes that would help it compete more effectively with rivals in the industrial gases sector, the sources said.
Air Liquide shares rose as much as 4.2% on the morning of August 31. The exact size of Elliott’s stake could not immediately be learned.
